newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Philippines' first lady to sing for HK handover.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' first lady to sing for HK handover.

text.p: Philippines' first lady Amelita Ramos is coming to sing at a party Hong Kong is throwing for the territory's more than 150,000 Asian domestic workers to mark its return to Chinese rule, organisers said on Wednesday.

Ramos, wife of Philippine President Fidel Ramos, will perform along with such famous Filipino singers as Martin Nievera and Pops Fernandez at the two-day party, set for June 29 and 30 in Kowloon Park, on the peninsula facing Hong Kong island.

"The colourful event is a gift for all the foreign domestic helpers in Hong Kong who give a big help to our women so that they can concentrate on their career," said Shelley Lau, Hong Kong's Director for Home Affairs, whose department is one of the organisers.
Other attractions at the event include live band performances, a beauty pageant and singing and dancing contests.
International stars like Bananarama, Mango Groove and Freebee are also due to perform.
The party takes place on the final two days before Hong Kong reverts to China. Organisers expected it to attract 65,000 people each day.
Most of the 150,000 Asian "amahs" working in Hong Kong come from the Philippines, Thailand or Indonesia.
